title: Waltz with Bashir
events_chronological: As a young conscript, Ari lands on the coast with an armoured column.
Ari's unit fires all night at a car approaching a roadblock and finds a family inside it in the morning.
A soldier called Carmi swims out to sea from a burning landing craft and survives when the rest of his unit does not.
A soldier named Frenkel dances with a machine gun down a boulevard under sniper fire, beneath posters of the assassinated president-elect.
Ari's unit shells an orchard and a boy with a rocket launcher is killed in front of them.
Ari and two others bathe in the sea at night under flares while the city burns behind them.
Militia enter the refugee camps while the army lights the sky above them.
Over two days the militia kill the people in the camps, while the soldiers on the rooftops fail to understand what they are watching.
Ari stands at the edge of the camp as the women come out screaming.
Twenty-four years later a friend tells Ari over a drink about a recurring dream of twenty-six dogs.
Ari realises he remembers nothing at all of the war and goes looking for the men he served with.
A psychologist explains to Ari that memory can be built out of what a person needs rather than what happened.
A television reporter tells Ari what he saw in the camps and what he said to the defence minister on the telephone.
Ari understands that the flare-lit memory of himself in the sea is a screen he built to stand between himself and the camps.
syuzhet_notes: The film moves between the present-day interviews, the war as each man recalls it, and dreams that turn out to be inventions, with no marker distinguishing them. Some scenes are established as false memories after they have been shown as fact.
fabula_notes: The war chronology is fixed by the campaign's own sequence. The present-day interviews are undated relative to each other, and the sea scene is placed where the film finally establishes it belongs.
